subject: general
question: A convex lens forms a real image of an object placed at a distance of 30 cm from it. If the image is formed at 60 cm on the other side of the lens, the focal length of the lens is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**20 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the **focal length** of the lens, we use the **Lens Formula**, which is expressed as **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**.
 
• According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **object distance (u)** is always taken as negative because the object is placed to the left of the lens. Therefore, **u = -30 cm**.
 
• Since the lens forms a **real image** on the other side of the lens, the **image distance (v)** is positive. Therefore, **v = +60 cm**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **1/f = 1/60 - 1/(-30)**. This simplifies to **1/f = 1/60 + 1/30**.
 
• Finding a common denominator, we get **1/f = (1 + 2) / 60**, which results in **1/f = 3/60**.
 
• By taking the reciprocal, we find the **focal length (f) = 60 / 3 = 20 cm**. ***Hence, the calculation shows the focal length is 20 cm.***
 
• The positive sign of the focal length confirms that the lens used is a **convex lens**, as they have **positive focal lengths**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is 20 cm.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convex Lens (Converging Lens):**
 
 
• A **convex lens** is thicker at the center than at the edges. It converges parallel rays of light passing through it.
 
• It can form both **real and virtual images** depending on the position of the object relative to the **optical center** and the **principal focus**.
 
• When the object is placed beyond the **focal point (F)**, the image formed is **real and inverted**.
 
 
 
• **Sign Convention for Lenses:**
 
 
• All distances are measured from the **optical center** of the lens.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of incident light are **positive**, while those measured against the direction of incident light are **negative**.
 
• The **focal length** of a **convex lens** is always **positive**, whereas for a **concave lens**, it is always **negative**.
 
 
 
• **Magnification (m):**
 
 
• **Magnification** is defined as the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object, or the ratio of **image distance (v)** to **object distance (u)**.
 
• Formula: **m = v / u**. In this specific case, **m = 60 / (-30) = -2**.
 
• A **negative magnification** indicates that the image is **real and inverted**. The numerical value **2** indicates that the image is **magnified** (twice the size of the object).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Power of a Lens:** The **power (P)** of a lens is the reciprocal of its focal length measured in **meters**. The **SI unit** of power is the **Dioptre (D)**. For this lens, the focal length is **0.2 meters**, so the power would be **P = 1 / 0.2 = +5 D**.
 
• **Nature of Image:** Since the **image distance** is positive and the image is formed on the side opposite to the object, the image is **real**. All real images formed by a single lens are **inverted**.
 
• **Object at 2F:** If an object is placed at **2f** (twice the focal length), the image is formed at **2f** on the other side. In this problem, **2f** would be **40 cm**. Since the object is at **30 cm** (between **f** and **2f**), the image is formed beyond **2f** (which **60 cm** is).
